newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mixed, mogas down $2 but CFDs up 5.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mixed, mogas down $2 but CFDs up 5.

text.p: European oil swaps were mixed on Wednesday as weaker oil futures made a partial recovery later.
Gasoline sunk $2 a tonne, fuel was down $1 but Brent crude CFDs edged higher and crack spreads against Brent were well bid.
Gasoline fell $2 a tonne for May swaps and nearer $4 for June after physical barges traded some $3 below Tuesday levels.
Gasoline crack spreads against Brent were little changed with June at $4.95 a barrel and the third and fourth quarters were pegged around $4.10 and $3.10 respectively.
Gas oil against Brent remained well bid but levels were little changed from Tuesday at $4.35 a barrel on the third quarter and $4.85 on the fourth.

Heavy fuel eased $1 a tonne to $82 for May and $87 for low sulphur. Dealers said the market remains bearish in Europe but further losses were unlikely due to firm levels in Singapore where May was pegged around $97.50 earlier on Wednesday.

Brent CFDs edged five cents higher to 58 cents under June for next week's dates. Dealers said a lack of buying had stalled physical crude markets but premiums had held steady. Wet Brent remained around 48 cents under May or the equivalent of 76 cents under June.
